Watch builds keep old assets `importedAssetsFromFileUrl` survives watch rebuilds and only adds files. With a fixed `entryFileNames` such as `entry.js`, removing or changing a non-inlined asset leaves its old filename in this set. `renderChunk` copies that filename into the new `importedAssets`, so the build and SSR manifests list an asset the chunk no longer uses. New JS asset URL path has no covering test The change makes JS asset modules emit ROLLDOWN_FILE_URL expressions resolved by a new resolveFileUrl hook. A regression could go unnoticed in relative base, renderBuiltUrl, postfix handling or manifest importedAssets for JS asset imports. vite:asset resolveFileUrl blocks user plugins' resolveFileUrl hooks The change adds a resolveFileUrl hook to vite:asset during build. findings.text: CSS text changes case The case-insensitive match replaces every spelling with lowercase `style`, changing CSS string values. For example, `<style>@import './text.css';</style>` with `.x::before { content: "</STYLE>"; }` in the imported file and `build.cssMinify: false` now displays `</style>` instead of `</STYLE>`. Escape the slash while keeping the matched text's original case. ```suggestion css = css.replace(styleTagCloseRE, (match) => match.replace('/', '\\/'), ) ```

Style tag escape changes the case of matched text The regex matches `</style` in any case. The replacement always writes lowercase `<\/style`. This changes the value of CSS strings that use another case. An inline style imports a file with `content: "</STYLE>"`. The output is `"<\/style>"`, so the page shows `</style>` instead of `</STYLE>`. Keep the matched text and insert only the backslash, for example `css.replace(styleTagCloseRE, (m) => '<\\' + m.slice(1))`.

Style tag escape changes the letter case of matched text The regex matches `</style` in any letter case. The replacement is always lowercase `<\/style`. So the escape changes uppercase or mixed-case text inside CSS strings and selectors. An inline <style> holds `content: '<\/STYLE>'`. The minifier outputs "</STYLE>". The escape rewrites it to "<\/style>", so the page shows "</style>". Keep the matched text in the replacement. For example, use `(m) => '<\\' + m.slice(1)`.

Escaping `</style` changes uppercase tag text to lowercase The regex ignores case. The replacement is always the lowercase text `<\/style`. So an uppercase `</STYLE` inside a CSS string is rewritten in lowercase. An inline style has `content:'<\/STYLE>'`. Lightning CSS minifies it to "</STYLE>". The replace gives "<\/style>", so the page shows `</style>` instead of `</STYLE>`. Keep the matched text. For example, use `css.replace(styleTagCloseRE, (m) => '<\\/' + m.slice(2))`.

For example, apply the top-level input only when environments.client.input is undefined.

Plugin entries miss scanning The new scanner branch skips `pluginContainer.resolveId`. If a plugin maps the configured entry to another real file, the build works, but scanning checks the unresolved path with `fs.existsSync` and drops it. Its dependencies are not found ahead of time, and the new warning condition hides this skipped entry. Resolve configured inputs through plugins before checking whether their files exist. ```suggestion ```

Dep scan skips plugin resolution for top-level input The new resolvePath returns the top-level input as given and never calls pluginContainer.resolveId. The entry filter then drops paths that fs.existsSync cannot find, like an extensionless or aliased entry. The build still resolves these entries through the resolver plugins, but the dev dep scan finds no entries. Line 137 also suppresses the warning when input is set, so pre-bundling is skipped with no message. Pass the top-level input through pluginContainer.resolveId like build.rolldownOptions.input. Keep the warning when the entries end up empty.

Library entry receives raw input with escape backslashes resolveEnvironmentOptions passes the raw `options.input` to resolveBuildEnvironmentOptions, which copies it into `lib.entry`. That skips resolveInput, so escaped glob characters like `\[id]` keep their backslashes. A library whose entry file needs escaping, such as `src/[id].ts`, fails to build. The literal backslash path does not exist on disk. Pass the resolved input from resolveInput to resolveBuildEnvironmentOptions. Make the same change at the top-level call site.

Client environment input is concatenated instead of overridden resolveConfig puts `config.input` into defaultClientEnvironmentOptions and merges it with `environments.client` through root-level mergeConfig. The new mergeInput branch then joins the two values instead of letting the client value win. Suppose a user sets top-level `input: 'a.ts'` and `environments.client.input: 'b.ts'`. The client then builds and scans both entries, although per-environment input should override the top-level value. Set the client input after the merge, using the client environment value when it is defined. Another option is to skip mergeInput when merging environment defaults.

Merged inputs lose pages Merging `input: ['a/index.html', 'b/index.html']` with a named input silently drops `a/index.html`. `normalizeToInputObject` gives both paths the key `index`, and `Object.fromEntries` keeps only the last one. Preserve every unnamed entry when converting an array to named inputs, and add a same-basename test.

Default `lib.entry` uses raw input and keeps glob escapes The change copies the raw `input` into `lib.entry`. The raw value does not go through `unescapeGlobCharacters`. The normal build path uses the unescaped value, so the two paths differ. A config sets `input: 'src/\\[id].ts'` and `build.lib: {}`. On POSIX the lib entry resolves to `src/\[id].ts`, and the build cannot find the file. Use the resolved `input` from `resolveInput` as the default for `lib.entry`.

mergeInput drops entries that share a basename normalizeToInputObject keys each entry by its file basename. Entries with the same basename collide. One entry is lost without a warning. A user config has input ['pages/home/index.html','pages/about/index.html']. A plugin returns input {admin:'admin.html'}. The result has no home page entry. Detect key collisions and throw an error, or make the generated keys unique.

Escaped library entries fail The library default receives raw `options.input`, not the resolved value. For example, `input: 'src/\\*.ts'` correctly selects the literal file `src/*.ts` outside library mode, but an omitted `build.lib.entry` receives the escape backslash unchanged. Library builds then resolve a different filename and fail. Use the already-unescaped input when supplying the library default.

low correctness: Merging array input with record input drops entries that share a basename normalizeToInputObject uses the file basename without its extension as the key. Two entries with the same basename get the same key. Object.fromEntries keeps only the last one, and no warning shows. Failure: The user config sets input: ['src/a/index.ts', 'src/b/index.ts']. A plugin config hook returns input: { admin: 'src/admin.ts' }. The merged input is { index: 'src/b/index.ts', admin }, so src/a/index.ts is not built. Evidence: - `packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts:1558-1559`: `input.map((i) => [path.basename(i, path.extname(i)), i]),` - `packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts:1547-1549`: `...normalizeToInputObject(a),` Fix: Detect duplicate keys and throw an error, or make each key unique, for example from the path relative to the root.

Top-level input is ignored for `build.ssr: true` builds The docs say that `input` is the default entry when `build.ssr` is `true`. The SSR build runs in the `ssr` environment. Only the client environment gets the top-level `input`, so the build falls back to `index.html` and throws. A config sets `input: 'src/entry-server.ts'`, and the user runs `vite build --ssr`. The build throws because the SSR input is an html file. Pass the top-level `input` to the environment that a legacy `build.ssr` build uses. Or remove the `input` claim from the `build.ssr` docs.

Unescape step removes Windows path separators before special characters The regex removes a backslash before characters such as "@", "(" and "[". On Windows, that backslash is often a path separator. The resolved path then points to a different file. On Windows, input is "C:\work\@app\src\main.ts". The value becomes "C:\work@app\src\main.ts". The build and the scanner use a path that does not exist. Do not unescape absolute Windows paths, or normalize separators before you apply the unescape regex.

Input merge drops entries that share a basename normalizeToInputObject keys each path by its basename without the extension. Paths like `src/a/index.ts` and `src/b/index.ts` collide, and only the last one survives. When a string or array input is merged with a record input, entries are silently lost. The build and dependency scan then miss those entry points. Detect duplicate keys and either make them unique or throw an error that names the clashing paths.

Library entry uses the raw input without unescaping resolveBuildEnvironmentOptions copies the raw `options.input` into `lib.entry`. Pass the input after unescapeGlobCharacters has run, or the resolved environment input, into resolveBuildEnvironmentOptions.

SSR ignores the new input With `input: 'src/server.ts'` and `build.ssr: true`, the SSR build still selects `index.html` and throws. The new default sends `input` only to the client environment, but the updated docs promise that it also supplies the SSR entry. Forward it to the legacy SSR environment when `build.ssr` is `true`, while keeping ordinary environment inputs separate.

Client environment input concatenates with top-level input instead of overriding The change puts the top-level input into the client defaults. The defaults merge with mergeConfig at root path. That merge calls mergeInput, which joins two strings into an array. Config sets input 'src/main.ts' and environments.client.input 'src/other.ts'. The client builds both files and does not override. Do not put input in defaultClientEnvironmentOptions. After the merge, set client.input ??= config.input.

Entries with the same basename collide when merged into an object normalizeToInputObject keys each array entry by its file basename. Entries such as `src/a/index.ts` and `src/b/index.ts` both get the key `index`. When an array input is merged with an object input, all but one same-named entry is silently dropped. The build then misses entry points. Detect duplicate keys and make them unique, or throw an error that names the conflicting entries.

Later builds reuse old entries Assigning `merged.lib.entry` also changes the caller's `build.lib` object. `mergeWithDefaults` copies defaults, but keeps this supplied object by reference. The second build then ignores its own input and builds the first entry again. Copy `merged.lib` before adding the default. ```suggestion if (merged.lib && merged.lib.entry == null && input != null) { merged.lib = { ...merged.lib, entry: input } } ```
